$comment: Template starter for projects/{slug}/categories-config.json. Copy this file to projects/{slug}/categories-config.json and fill in the values. Validate against category-design-principles.md (one subcategory = one intent; no faceted dimensions as subcategories; 5-10 top-level; 2 levels deep; descriptions 35-80w plain prose).
note: Free-text editorial note. Reference the design doc if one exists (e.g. projects/{slug}/content-taxonomy.md).

categories.$comment: TOP-LEVEL EXAMPLE — duplicate this block for each of your 5-10 top-level categories. parent=null marks it as a top-level. Description 40-60w, no HTML, no inline links.
categories.name: Example Top-Level Category
categories.description: Two-sentence plain-prose description, 40-60 words. Sentence 1 = what kind of content + target persona. Sentence 2 = 2-3 specific topic markers + credibility-grounding clause. No HTML. No inline links. No inside-baseball ('E-E-A-T anchor', 'engineering pillar that anchors content', etc.).
categories.rank_math_title: Category Name: Differentiating Phrase | Brand Name
categories.rank_math_description: 150-160 character meta description. Focus keyword in first 120 chars. Plain text, no HTML.
categories.rank_math_focus_keyword: primary keyword, secondary keyword, tertiary keyword
categories.rank_math_facebook_title: Shorter OG title for social sharing
categories.rank_math_facebook_description: Shorter OG description (110-130 chars) for Facebook/LinkedIn shares

categories.$comment: SUBCATEGORY EXAMPLE — parent=slug-of-the-top-level (NOT the integer WP id; the setup script resolves IDs from slugs at apply time). Description 35-50w. Single primary intent (Informational / Commercial-Investigation / Transactional). Subcategories ARE content-type axes, NOT facets — do not create 'by-wattage' or 'by-crop' subcategories; use tags for those.
categories.name: Buyer Guides
categories.description: Single-product decision content for [PRODUCT FAMILY] — by [ATTRIBUTE], [ATTRIBUTE], and use case. Evaluation criteria: [SPECIFIC SPEC 1], [SPECIFIC SPEC 2], [SPECIFIC SPEC 3], and warranty terms.
categories.rank_math_title: Best [PRODUCT FAMILY] Buyer Guides | Brand Name
categories.rank_math_description: Single-product [PRODUCT FAMILY] buyer guides by [ATTRIBUTE], form factor, and use case. [Brand-specific differentiator].
categories.rank_math_facebook_description: Single-product [PRODUCT FAMILY] buyer guides by attribute, form factor, and use case.
categories.rank_math_twitter_description: Buyer guides by [ATTRIBUTE], form factor, and use case for [target persona].

_design_notes.intent_classification: Every subcategory must map to exactly ONE primary intent. Informational = definitions/how-to/science/calculator/glossary. Commercial-Investigation = buyer guide/comparison/roundup. Transactional = product detail/pricing (typically lives in Woocommerce product_cat, not here).
_design_notes.content_types_not_facets: Use subcategories for content TYPE (Buyer Guides, Comparisons, How-To, Calculators, Glossary, Deep Dives). Do NOT use them for faceted dimensions (wattage, crop, brand, region) — those are TAGS.
_design_notes.slug_uniqueness: WordPress requires globally unique slugs. Use parent-prefixed slugs (e.g. 'lighting-buyer-guides', 'climate-buyer-guides') so 'Buyer Guides' under multiple parents doesn't collide.
_design_notes.description_length: 35-80 words. Plain prose. No HTML, no inline links. The post grid below the description already shows links to specific articles — duplicating them inline is cannibalization.
_design_notes.banned_phrases: Do NOT use: 'E-E-A-T anchor', 'engineering pillar that anchors', 'topical authority', 'pillar-spoke', 'crawl budget', 'optimized for AI/search', 'demoted to lower-priority linking'. These are content-strategy terms that should not appear in user-facing copy.
